Bake in preheated 350°F oven for 16 to 20 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out slightly sticky. Cool completely.

recipes.title: Blueberry Coconut Muffins
recipes.description: Light muffins with blueberries and shredded coconut.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. In a medium bowl, mix flour, sugars and baking powder. In another bowl lightly mix milk and yogurt.
Add egg, oil and vanilla to wet mixture. Be careful to not over mix. Make a well in the dry mixture and add the wet mixture. Gently fold together.
Add blueberries and coconut to dough and combine until just blended.
Fill greased and floured muffin tins about 3/4 full. Bake for 20 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean of the middle.

recipes.title: Raspberry Lemon Muffins
recipes.description: Tangy lemon muffins studded with fresh raspberries.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees. Line muffin tins with paper liners. In a medium bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt and pudding.
Lightly whisk eggs in another bowl. Add buttermilk, vanilla and oil. Zest the lemons and set aside. Juice the lemons and combine to wet mixture.
Combine the milk mixture with the flour mixture and fold together, being careful not to over mix. Add the lemon zest and fold in raspberries.
Fill muffin tins about 3/4 full and bake for about 20 minutes or until done in the middle.

recipes.title: Southern Corn Muffins
recipes.description: Savory corn muffins with taco seasoning and dill.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Grease and flour muffin tins.
Combine flour with the corn meal. Add to the flour the baking powder and salt. In a medium bowl whisk together the sugar, egg, honey and oil until just mixed.
Alternate combining milk and corn into the egg mixture. Create a well in the middle of the dry ingredients and fold in the wet ingredients. Add the taco seasoning and mix until just combined.
Fill the muffin tins till about 3/4 full. Top the batter with a sprinkling of dill in each cup. Bake for about 20-25 minutes or until golden brown and done in the middle.

recipes.title: Traditional Blueberry Muffins
recipes.description: Classic buttermilk blueberry muffins with optional walnuts.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Grease muffin tins with shortening.

Combine flour, salt, baking powder and baking soda in a bowl. In another bowl combine sugar with egg and vanilla. Once butter is cooled add to the sugar mixture. Add buttermilk. Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and just combine.
Batter will be slightly lumpy. Fold in blueberries and walnuts. Spoon batter into prepared muffin tins and bake until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean, about 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Banana Nut Breakfast Muffins
recipes.description: Hearty whole wheat muffins with bananas, oats, and pecans.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees. Prepare muffin tins by either greasing tins with shortening or by filling with muffin papers. In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, baking powder and baking soda. Set aside.

In a medium bowl, combine sugars with egg and oil. Add to the wet mixture the yogurt and bananas. Combine wet ingredients with dry ingredients until just mixed. Overworking the batter will cause the batter to be too hard.
Add the oats and pecans. Spoon batter into muffin tins. Bake for about 20 minutes or until a toothpick comes out of the center clean.

recipes.title: Morning Start Blueberry Oatmeal Muffins
recipes.description: Wholesome breakfast muffins with blueberries, oats, and pecans.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. In one bowl combine the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
In another bowl combine the sugar, egg and vanilla. Add to the wet ingredients the yogurt and milk. Combine the wet ingredients with the dry and fold in blueberries, oats and pecans until just mixed.
Spoon batter into prepared muffin tins and bake for about 20 minutes or until done in the middle.

recipes.title: Honey Lavender Muffins
recipes.description: Elegant muffins infused with culinary lavender and honey.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees. Grease muffin tins with shortening.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt in a medium bowl. In another bowl combine sugar, egg and butter (cooled). Once lightly mixed, add the yogurt, milk and honey.

Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and sprinkle in the lavender and lemon zest. Scoop batter into muffin tins and bake for about 20 minutes or until done in the middle. Serve warm with your favorite jam and honey butter.

recipes.title: Chai Spiced Muffins
recipes.description: Warmly spiced muffins with cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, and allspice.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugars, baking powder, salt and spices.

In another bowl lightly whisk the egg, vanilla, milk and oil. Combine all ingredients together and lightly mix. Bake for about 20-25 minutes or until golden brown and a tooth pick inserted in the center comes out clean.
These muffins are perfect for cozy days at home with something warm to drink!

recipes.title: Healthy Bran Apple Muffins
recipes.description: Fiber-rich muffins with wheat bran, apples, and pecans.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Prepare muffin tins by greasing them with cooking spray or use muffin papers.
Chop 1/2 cup pecans and set aside. Reserve the other half cup as whole pecans; set aside.
In a large bowl, combine flour, bran, salt and baking powder; set aside.

In another bowl combine egg, brown sugar and applesauce. When mixed, add milk, yogurt and oil. Combine the egg mixture with the flour mixture, fold in chopped pecans and apples. Scoop into muffin tins and top each muffin with a whole pecan.
Bake for 20-25 minutes or until done in the middle.

recipes.title: Honey Bran Muffins
recipes.description: Wholesome bran muffins sweetened with honey and studded with raisins.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Combine flour, bran, salt, baking powder and brown sugar in a large bowl. Combine the honey and butter together with a fork.
When smooth, add the buttermilk and eggs. Bring the flour mixture and honey mixture together and stir till just combined. Add the raisins and combine.
Spoon batter into greased muffin tins. Bake for about 20-25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean. Cool and serve.

recipes.title: Wholewheat Maple Bread
recipes.description: Hearty oatmeal bread sweetened with maple sugar and syrup.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 360 degrees.
Mix boiling water, oats, maple sugar, maple syrup, butter, salt, and cinnamon in a large mixing bowl. Let cool.
When mix is cooled, add yeast, whole wheat flour, and all-purpose flour and mix to form a dough.
Knead for 10 minutes or until dough is smooth.
Coat a bowl with oil. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with oil.
Cover and allow to sit for 1 hour.
Split dough in half and shape each into a bread loaf.
Place loaves in greased pans, cover and let sit in pans for 1 hour.
Brush loaves with water and dust rolled oats over the loaves.
Bake 30 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Wholegrain Seed Bread
recipes.description: Crusty whole wheat bread packed with mixed seeds.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Mix 3-1/2 cups whole wheat flour, sugar, and salt in large bowl.
Make a well in the middle with your hand. Place yeast in the well and cover yeast with 1 cup lukewarm water.
Add 1 tbsp flour. Let sit for 10 minutes or until it begins to bubble.
Form the dough by scraping flour into the yeast hole slowly and mixing well.
Stir in 1 cup of seeds and mix well. Dough should be sticky but if too sticky, add a bit of flour.
Spread flour on work surface. Knead dough for 5-10 minutes or until it isn't sticky anymore.
Cover and let sit for 1 hour or until dough doubles.
Place dough on floured work space (add more flour to surface if needed). Gently punch down dough with your fist or palm.
Shape into a ball. Roll ball in 1/2 cup of seeds and place in oiled and floured baking pan.
Cover and let sit for 1 hour or until dough doubles.
Bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Wholewheat Honey Bread
recipes.description: Soft whole wheat bread sweetened with honey, shaped into torpedo loaves.

instructions.text: Mix flours, yeast, and salt in large bowl.
Add 1 cup milk, water, honey, butter, and shortening. Mix well.
Knead dough for 10-15 minutes. Dough will be like elastic. Add small bits of flour if needed.
Cover with dishcloth and let sit for 5 minutes. Knead again.
Coat a bowl with oil. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with oil on all sides.
Cover again and let sit until doubled or about 1 1/2 - 2 hours.
Dip hands in flour and gently punch down dough.
Divide dough into thirds. Roll first piece lengthwise into torpedo shape.
Use a knife to cut two slashes in the top of each loaf. Repeat with other two dough pieces.
Place on baking sheet covered with parchment paper. Let rise for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle each loaf with a bit of water and bake for 10 minutes. Occasionally sprinkle water over each loaf.
Turn temperature down to 325 degrees and bake for another 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Unbleached Ciabatta Bread
recipes.description: Rustic Italian ciabatta bread made with sourdough starter.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 390 degrees.
Mix yeast in starter and water. Let stand for 10 minutes.
Stir in milk, olive oil, and salt. Add flour one cup at a time.
Spread flour on work surface. Cover with dishtowel and let sit for 20 minutes.
Coat a bowl with oil. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with oil.
Cover dough with dishtowel and let sit for about 2 hours or until it doubles in size.
Gently punch dough down until it folds over. Form into a ball.
Cover and let sit until it doubles again.
On floured work surface, divide the dough into thirds.
Form first piece into a rectangular shape. Fold down the top. Fold up the bottom. Roll strip into a log shape.
Gently seal the seam with a pinch of water. Fold dough three times. Repeat with other two pieces.
Roll baguettes over floured surface until they stretch out and become longer.
Place on floured baking sheet. Cover with cloth and let sit for 1/2 hour or until plumped up.
Use a knife to cut two vertical slashes in the top of each baguette. Sprinkle baguettes with water.
Add a small pan of hot water to bottom rack of oven.
Bake for 10-12 minutes. Reduce temperature to 300 degrees and bake for 25 minutes or until golden brown.

notes: Sourdough starter can be ordered from Amazon

recipes.title: Unbleached Baguettes
recipes.description: Classic French baguettes with a sweet egg wash topping.

instructions.text: Mix yeast and water well. Let stand for 3 minutes.
Mix flour and salt in a large bowl. Add yeast mix and cool water.
Knead dough with your hands. Spread flour over work area. Knead dough for about 4 minutes.
Flour your hands and separate dough in two pieces.
Form bread and place on baking sheet. Lightly sprinkle flour over both loaves.
Let rest for 30 minutes.
Use a knife to cut two slashes in the top of each loaf.
Add a small pan of water to bottom rack of oven, as this helps with forming a crust on the loaves.
Rub loaves with 1 beaten egg and top with 2 tbsp sugar.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Sweet Finnish Pulla
recipes.description: Traditional Finnish cardamom-spiced braided bread with sugar topping.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 390 degrees.
In small saucepan, heat milk until warm. Set aside.
In warm water, dissolve yeast. Add warm milk, sugar, salt, cardamom, 4 beaten eggs, and about 2 cups flour. Mix well.
Dough should be smooth and elastic. Add 3 cups flour and butter. Mix well until dough is glossy.
Prepare floured work surface. Knead dough. Cover and let sit for 15 minutes.
Coat a bowl with oil. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with oil.
Cover and let sit for 15 minutes or until doubled.
Gently punch down dough and set aside to rise once more.
On floured surface, divide dough into thirds. Divide each third into thirds again.
Form a 12-16 inch strip out of each piece. Take 3 strips and braid.
Repeat with other strips until you have 3 braided loaves.
Grease baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray. Place braided loaves onto baking sheet.
Set aside to rise for 20 minutes.
Rub loaves with 1 beaten egg and top with 2 tbsp sugar.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

notes: Traditional Finnish bread, often served at Christmas and Easter

recipes.title: Hungarian Cinnamon Swirl Bread
recipes.description: Sweet yeast bread with a cinnamon-brown sugar swirl.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Combine flour, sugar, salt, and yeast in large bowl.
Mix well. Stir in egg, melted butter, warm milk, and vanilla extract.
Mix well until dough is smooth and elastic.
Coat a bowl with oil. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with oil.
Cover and let sit for 1 1/2 hours or until doubled.
Gently punch down dough and set aside to rise once more.
Gently punch down dough. On floured surface, divide dough in half.
Form each piece into a 1/3 inch thick rectangular shape.
Spread melted butter over each rectangle.
In small bowl, stir together cinnamon and brown sugar. Sprinkle cinnamon sugar over each buttered loaf.
Roll loaves into log shapes and seal the ends by pinching gently and tucking ends under.
Grease glass pan, place loaves in pan, and cover.
Set aside to rise for 45 minutes or until doubled.
Spread melted butter over tops of loaves and bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Oatmeal Molasses Rolls
recipes.description: Hearty rolls with oats and molasses, topped with butter and oats.

instructions.text: Mix yeast with 1/4 cup lukewarm water and a pinch of sugar until it bubbles.
In a separate bowl, combine scalded milk and butter and mix until butter melts.
Stir in brown sugar, oats, molasses, and salt and mix well.
Set aside and cool to room temperature.
Stir in egg and add yeast mix. Mix well.
Add 2 1/2 cups flour and mix well. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Coat a bowl with oil. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with oil.
Chill in refrigerator for 2 hours or more.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Spread flour on work surface. With floured hands, knead dough and form into 12 balls.
Form each ball into a rectangle, roll into a log and tuck under the ends.
Butter the bottom of a 9-inch round pan.
Spread butter and oats over each roll.
Set aside and let sit for 2 hours or until dough doubles.
Bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Panettone
recipes.description: Italian sweet bread with dried currants and raisins, traditionally served at Christmas.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix yeast, water, and sugar in medium bowl. Cover and set aside for 10 minutes or until it foams.
Stir in eggs, yogurt, vanilla, lemon zest, and salt and mix well.
Add in flour slowly and mix until dough forms.
On floured workspace, knead dough for 5-10 minutes or until smooth and elastic. Add a little flour as needed to reach desired consistency.
Spray a bowl with nonstick cooking spray or oil. Place dough in bowl, cover, and set aside to rise for 1 hour or until dough doubles in size.
Mix fruit (currants and raisins) and confectioners' sugar in a small bowl.
Punch dough down and place on floured workspace. Gently add the fruit to the dough.
Shape dough into a ball, place in 8-inch cake pan sprayed with nonstick cooking spray, cover, and set aside to rise for 30 minutes.
Rub loaf with melted butter and bake for 45 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Honey Oatmeal Bread
recipes.description: Sweet cinnamon swirl bread topped with butter and oats.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Combine flour, sugar, salt, and yeast in large bowl. Mix well.
Stir in egg, melted butter, warm milk, and vanilla extract.
Mix well until dough is smooth and elastic.
Coat a bowl with oil. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with oil.
Cover and let sit for 1 1/2 hours or until doubled.
Gently punch down dough and set aside to rise once more.
Gently punch down dough. On floured surface, divide dough in half.
Form each piece into a 1/3 inch thick rectangular shape.
Spread melted butter over each rectangle.
In small bowl, stir together cinnamon and brown sugar. Sprinkle cinnamon sugar over each buttered loaf.
Roll loaves into log shapes and seal the ends by pinching gently and tucking ends under.
Grease glass pan, place loaves in pan, and cover.
Set aside to rise for 45 minutes or until doubled.
Spread melted butter and oats over tops of loaves and bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown.

notes: Similar to Hungarian Cinnamon Swirl Bread but topped with oats
Despite the name, this recipe contains no honey
recipes.variant_notes: Same base recipe, but topped with butter and oats instead of butter only

recipes.title: Gruyère, Pepper & Onion Bread
recipes.description: Savory yeast bread stuffed with sautéed peppers, onions, and Gruyère cheese.

ingredients.prep_note: sliced, preferably red and yellow mixed

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix 3 1/2 cups flour, salt, and sugar in large bowl.
Add 2 tbsp olive oil.
Make a well in the mixture with your hand. Place yeast in the empty space and cover yeast with 1 cup lukewarm water.
Add 1 tbsp flour. Let sit for 10 minutes or until it begins to bubble.
Form the dough by scraping flour into the yeast hole slowly and mixing well. Dough should be sticky but if too sticky, add a bit of flour.
Spread flour on work surface. Knead dough for 5-10 minutes or until it isn't sticky anymore.
Cover and let sit for 1 hour or until dough doubles.
In remainder of oil, sauté onion, bell peppers, and cayenne pepper until soft. Drain on napkin and let cool.
Place dough on floured work space (add more flour to surface if needed).
Gently punch down dough with your fist or palm.
Add vegetables and cheese to the dough. Shape dough into a ball.
Cover and let sit for 1 hour or until dough doubles.
Spread beaten egg over top of bread.
Bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Garlic Artisan Bread
recipes.description: Rustic artisan loaves made with roasted garlic and whole wheat flour, brushed with garlic butter.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Puree garlic heads. Blend in butter until creamy.
Add yeast and water. Mix. Stir in salt.
Add flour in parts - wheat flour, then unbleached flour. Mix well.
Spread flour on work surface. Knead dough for 10-15 minutes. Dough will be like elastic. Add small bits of flour if needed.
Cover with dishcloth and let sit for 5 minutes. Knead again.
Coat bowl with butter. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with butter on all sides.
Cover again and let sit until doubled.
Dip hands in flour and gently punch down dough. Divide dough into thirds. Form into balls.
With a rolling pin, roll out one ball into a rectangular shape about 7 inches x 14 inches.
Brush rectangle dough with garlic butter. Roll up lengthwise.
Seal ends of dough with a little pinch. Repeat with other two dough balls.
Cover baking sheet(s) with cornmeal. Place dough on baking sheet(s).
Use a knife to cut two slashes in the top of each loaf.
Add a small pan of water to bottom rack of oven, as this helps with forming a crust on the loaves.
Bake for 35-40 minutes. Occasionally sprinkle cold water over each loaf.

notes: Pan of water in oven helps form crust
Sprinkle cold water on loaves during baking for crusty exterior

recipes.title: Cinnamon Raisin Bread
recipes.description: Sweet yeast bread swirled with cinnamon, brown sugar, and raisins.

instructions.text: Mix brown sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. Cover and set to one side.
Mix flour, sugar, yeast, and salt in large bowl.
Add egg, milk, water, and 2 tbsp melted butter. Mix well.
Cover and let sit for 2-3 hours or until dough doubles.
Chill for 3 hours or more.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Spread flour on work surface. Dip hands in flour and roll dough on work surface.
Form an 8 inch x 10 inch rectangle.
Brush with half of remaining melted butter and sprinkle brown sugar cinnamon mixture over the loaf.
Top with raisins.
Roll dough into a tubular shape. Seal the ends and place in loaf pan sprayed with nonstick cooking spray.
Brush remaining butter over the top and let sit for 45 minutes.
Bake for 50 minutes or until golden brown.

notes: Requires 3+ hours chilling time

recipes.title: Fougasse
recipes.description: Traditional Provençal flatbread with herbs, shaped like a leaf with decorative slits.

instructions.text: Dissolve yeast in water.
Add 1 cup flour, half of the dried herbs, sea salt, and 2 tbsp oil. Mix well.
For the remaining 2 cups of flour, add one cup of flour at a time until dough is proper consistency.
On floured workspace, knead dough until smooth and elastic.
Coat a bowl with oil. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with oil. Coat all surfaces of dough with the oil.
Cover and let sit for 1 hour or until doubled.
Gently punch down dough. Divide dough in half. Form dough into ovals.
Dust two cooking sheets with cornmeal. Place oval dough forms on sheets.
Rub dough with 2 tbsp olive oil and remaining herbs.
Cut slits in the loaves with a knife.
Cover and set aside to rise for 20 minutes or until doubled.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
When hot, create steam by splashing a little water on the bottom of the oven.
Place baking sheets with loaves in the oven and close the door.
Bake for 20 minutes or until golden brown.

notes: Steam in oven helps create crusty exterior
Traditional leaf shape with decorative slits

recipes.title: French Chocolate Bread
recipes.description: Rich sweet bread filled with chocolate ganache and topped with a cinnamon streusel.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix yeast and warm water in a large bowl.
Stir in butter, sugar, egg yolks, milk, and salt. Mix thoroughly.
Slowly add flour until a soft dough forms.
On floured workspace, knead dough until smooth and elastic.
Coat a bowl with oil. Gently roll dough in bowl until covered with oil.
Cover and let sit for 1 hour or until doubled.
While dough is rising, prepare filling: Place chocolate chips, milk, and sugar in a small saucepan and cook over low heat until creamy and smooth. Add cinnamon and stir. Set aside.
Prepare topping: Mix flour, sugar, and cinnamon in a small bowl and cut in butter. Topping mix should be crumbly. Add chocolate chips and nuts to topping mix. Set aside.
Gently punch down dough. Form into 18 inch x 10 inch rectangle and spread the filling mix over the dough.
From long side of rectangle, roll up dough into a tube and pinch the ends and seam to seal.
Spray 10 inch fluted pan with nonstick cooking spray and place tube carefully in the pan.
Add the topping to the bread, cover and set aside to rise for 30 minutes or until doubled.
Bake for 45-50 minutes or until golden brown.
Top baked bread with confectioners' sugar when cooled.

recipes.title: Chocolate Cinnamon Babka
recipes.description: Rich braided bread with chocolate cinnamon filling and streusel topping.

instructions.text: In small bowl, heat milk and 1/4 cup butter until warm.
In another bowl, mix bread flour, 2 cups all-purpose flour, yeast, and 1/4 cup sugar.
Add water, warm milk mixture (from first bowl), egg, and salt.
Knead dough until smooth and elastic. Add flour as needed for consistency.
Cover and set aside to rise for 1 1/2 hours or until doubled.
While dough rises, prepare filling: Stir chopped chocolate, cinnamon, and 1/3 cup sugar. Cut in 1/4 cup butter. Set aside.
Prepare streusel: Mix confectioners' sugar and 1/4 cup flour together. Cut in 1/4 cup butter to form crumbs.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Gently punch down dough. On floured surface, divide dough in half. Form each piece into a ball.
Cover and let sit for 10 minutes.
On floured workspace, shape each ball into a 15 inch x 4 inch rectangle.
Spread half the filling on each rectangle.
Form logs by rolling each ball and sealing seams.
Form a circle with each log on baking sheet.
Carefully slash top of circle with slits one inch apart.
Cover and let sit for 30 minutes or until doubled.
Sprinkle streusel on top of loaves.
Bake for 25 minutes or until golden brown.

notes: Formed into circles with decorative slits on top

recipes.title: Seafood Specialty
recipes.source_note: MomMom's cookbook, page 46 - printed community cookbook
recipes.description: A rich baked casserole with shrimp, tuna, crabmeat, and mushrooms in a creamy base.

instructions.text: Cook soup and rice in water until tender.
Saute celery, onion, and pepper in margarine.
Combine all ingredients.
Top with sliced almonds, grated Cheddar, and paprika.
Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Seafood Stew
recipes.source_note: MomMom's cookbook, page 46 - printed community cookbook
recipes.description: A hearty stew with salt pork, potatoes, shrimp, and whitefish in a tomato base.

instructions.text: In a large saucepot, cook salt pork until crisp. Remove pork and reserve.
Add onion, green pepper, and celery and saute about 5 minutes.
Add reserved pork, potatoes, tomatoes, and seasonings.
Cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Add shrimp, fish, and scallops and simmer 10 minutes longer.

recipes.title: All Seasons Pesto Spaghetti
recipes.source_note: MomMom's cookbook, page 46 - printed community cookbook
recipes.description: A quick pesto pasta with dried basil that can be made year-round.

instructions.text: Mix water and basil; set aside for 30 minutes.
Heat margarine and garlic until margarine melts.
Remove from heat.
Whisk in basil mixture, lemon juice, parsley, and cheese.
Toss with hot, cooked spaghetti, and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Beef Manicotti
recipes.source_note: MomMom's cookbook, page 47 - printed community cookbook
recipes.description: Stuffed manicotti shells with ground beef, Mozzarella, and Italian seasonings baked in tomato sauce.

instructions.text: Cook ground beef and 1/4 cup onion in 10 inch skillet, stirring frequently; drain.
Stir in bread, 1 1/2 cups Mozzarella, egg, milk, parsley, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Fill uncooked manicotti shells, packing beef into both ends.
Place shells in ungreased 13x9x2 inch pan.
Heat remaining ingredients, except Parmesan cheese, to boiling in Dutch oven, stirring occasionally; reduce heat.
Simmer, uncovered, 5 minutes.
Pour sauce over shells.
Cover and bake in 375° oven 1 1/2 hours to 1 3/4 hours, or until shells are tender.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.

recipes.title: Impossible Lasagne Pie
recipes.source_note: MomMom's cookbook, page 47 - printed community cookbook
recipes.description: A crustless 'impossible' pie with lasagna flavors - ground beef, cottage cheese, and Italian herbs.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 400°.
Grease pie plate, 10 x 1 1/2 inches.
Layer cottage and Parmesan cheese in plate.
Mix beef, herbs, paste, and 1/2 cup Mozzarella.
Spoon on top.
Beat milk, baking mix, eggs, salt, and pepper 15 seconds in blender on high or 1 minute with hand blender.
Pour into plate.
Bake until knife inserted between center and edge comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining Mozzarella.

recipes.title: Italian Stir-Fry
recipes.source_note: MomMom's cookbook, page 47 - printed community cookbook
recipes.description: A quick pasta dish with fresh vegetables, herbs, and two cheeses.

instructions.text: Cook pasta. Set aside.
Prepare all vegetables.
In stir-fry pan or wok, heat oil.
Add crushed garlic.
Add zucchini and onion.
Stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add parsley, tomatoes, basil, pasta, Parmesan, and Mozzarella.
Toss gently.
Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Tofu Techniques
recipes.description: How to prepare and cut tofu for cooking.

instructions.text: Remove tofu from water or packaging. Place on toweling and pat to dry.
Cut tofu into 1/2-inch slices. Turn, slice into 1/2-inch strips, then into uniform cubes.

notes: These techniques work for extra-firm tofu used in stir-fries and other dishes.

recipes.title: Food Safety Tips - Power Outage
recipes.description: Don't Touch That Door! What to do when the power goes out.

instructions.text: If the power goes out, food will remain chilled for up to 6 hours as long as you don't open the refrigerator door.
Butter, margarine, hard or processed cheeses, and fresh vegetables and fruits will keep at room temperature for a few days; other perishables should be discarded.
Food in a full, closed freezer will be O.K. for about 2 days; a half-full freezer roughly 1 day.

recipes.title: Fruit and Cream Pie Tips
recipes.description: Tips for making fruit and cream pies with graham cracker crust.

instructions.text: Press graham cracker-butter mixture into bottom and up sides of pie plate.
Bake; let cool slightly. Use spatula to spread cream cheese mixture over bottom. Refrigerate.
Bring gelatin, pudding mix and water to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring constantly.
Arrange sliced fruit in decorative circles over cream cheese mixture; let pieces overlap slightly.

recipes.title: Sheila Farris's Chocolate Pie
recipes.source_note: Family Circle magazine, Blue Ribbon Pies - printed clipping
recipes.description: A rich chocolate cream pie with unsweetened cocoa powder.

instructions.text: Unfold piecrust; fit into 9-inch pie pan. Prebake according to package directions. Remove from oven. Reduce temperature to 350°.

Mix 1 1/2 cups sugar, the flour and cocoa in medium-size heavy-bottomed saucepan. Stir in just enough milk to make paste; stir in remaining milk. Cook over medium heat, stirring, 10 to 12 minutes or until thickened.

recipes.title: Julia's Pastry
recipes.description: A rich pie crust pastry with sour cream.

instructions.text: Cut butter into flour.
[Additional instructions not visible on card]

notes: Card also contains notes for a pasta dish: chop garlic saute slowly, dice tomatoes, dice chicken, chop basil, cook pasta

recipes.title: Cookie Making Tips
recipes.description: Tips for baking perfect cookies.

instructions.text: Use shiny aluminum baking sheets without sides for golden brown cookies.
Turn on your oven to the required temperature 10-15 minutes before baking.
If a recipe states to grease the baking sheets, use shortening for best results.
For even baking, make cookies the same size and thickness.
Leave at least 2 inches around the baking sheet and the oven walls for good heat circulation. For best results, bake only one sheet of cookies at a time.

recipes.title: Bread + Butter Pickles
recipes.description: Classic bread and butter pickles with mustard and celery seed.

instructions.text: Slice cucumbers and onions.
Heat vinegar, sugar, mustard seed, celery seed, and turmeric.
Pack cucumbers and onions in jars.
Pour hot brine over cucumbers and seal.

recipes.title: Linda's Cream Pie
recipes.description: A simple no-bake cream cheese pie with Cool Whip in a graham cracker crust.

instructions.text: Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Pour into graham cracker crust.
Top with strawberries if desired.
Refrigerate until set.

recipes.title: Crunchy Chocolate Malt Cupcakes

instructions.text: Make the frosting: Sprinkle the sugar evenly in a large skillet and add the corn syrup. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring once or twice. Continue to boil, swirling the pan but not stirring, until the caramel is amber. Carefully pour in the heavy cream (it will splatter) and add the butter. Simmer, whisking constantly, until the caramel is smooth, about 2 minutes.

Combine both chocolates and the salt in a medium heatproof bowl. Pour the hot caramel over the chocolate and let stand until melted, about 5 minutes. Whisk until smooth and shiny, then cover and refrigerate until set, at least 4 hours or overnight.

Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375°F. Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper liners. Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Sift the malted milk and cocoa powders into another bowl.

Beat the sugar and butter in a large bowl with a mixer until light and fluffy, about 7 minutes. Add the malted milk powder mixture and beat until combined. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. With the mixer on low speed, add the flour mixture in three parts, alternating with the half-and-half in two parts, beginning and ending with flour.

Divide the batter evenly among the prepared cups, filling each about three-quarters of the way. Bake until a toothpick inserted into a cupcake comes out clean, 15 to 20 minutes. Let cool in the pans 10 minutes, then transfer the cupcakes to racks to cool completely.

Beat the chilled frosting with a mixer or whisk until thick, about 2 minutes, but don't overwhip. Spread on the cupcakes or transfer to a pastry bag with a star tip and pipe on top. Refrigerate until ready to serve, then sprinkle with the cereal.

notes: Can be made up to 2 days ahead.
Frosting can be stored 4 hours or overnight.
Refrigerate until ready to serve, then sprinkle with the cereal.

recipes.title: Coconut Cupcakes with Chocolate and Almonds

ingredients.item: large eggs plus 4 egg whites, at room temperature
unsalted butter, cut into pieces, at room temperature

instructions.text: Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 325°F. Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper liners. Whisk the whole eggs and egg whites in a large bowl. Whisk in the cream of coconut and the coconut and vanilla extracts until smooth.

Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Beat in the butter, one piece at a time, with a mixer on low speed until the mixture resembles coarse meal, 3 to 4 minutes. Add half the egg mixture, increase the speed to medium-high and beat until fluffy, about 1 minute. Beat in the remaining egg mixture until combined, scraping down the bowl as needed.

Divide the batter among the prepared cups, filling each about halfway. Bake until a toothpick inserted into a cupcake comes out clean, 18 to 22 minutes. Let cool in the pans 10 minutes; transfer to racks to cool completely.

Make the topping: Combine the milk, coconut, confectioners' sugar, vanilla and salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat and cook until the milk is absorbed and the mixture thickens, stirring occasionally, about 15 minutes. Cool completely.

Make the glaze: Put the chocolate, corn syrup, butter and 3 tablespoons hot water in a microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave on 50 percent power until the chocolate melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk to combine. Keep warm.

Top each cupcake with a heaping tablespoonful of the coconut mixture, pressing gently until compact. Spoon 1 teaspoon glaze on top and garnish with 2 almonds. Refrigerate until the glaze sets, about 20 minutes.

Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 300°F, using the convection setting, if available. Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper liners. Put the butter, cocoa powder and 1/4 cup water in a microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave until the butter melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk to combine, then whisk in the brown sugar.

Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Whisk in the warm cocoa mixture. In another bowl, beat the buttermilk, eggs and vanilla; stir into the batter until just combined but don't overmix.

Divide the batter among the prepared cups, filling each about three-quarters of the way. Bake until the cupcakes are slightly domed and spring back when lightly pressed, 25 to 30 minutes. Let cool in the pans 10 minutes, then transfer to racks to cool completely.

Make the brittle: Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper. Place the granulated sugar in a small saucepan over medium-high heat, bring to a boil and cook, swirling the pan but not stirring, until it turns amber. Remove from the heat; stir in the peanut butter and butterscotch chips until smooth. Immediately pour the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet, smooth into a thin brittle with a spatula and let cool. Break the brittle into pieces, place in a resealable plastic bag and crush with a rolling pin.

Make the frosting: Bring the cream to a simmer in a small saucepan. Remove from the heat, add the peanut butter chips and let stand about 5 minutes. Whisk until smooth. Place the pan over a bowl of ice, stirring occasionally, until the frosting is spreadable, about 10 minutes. Spread on the cupcakes or transfer to a pastry bag with a large round tip and pipe on top; sprinkle with the brittle.

ingredients.item: chopped salted roasted peanuts, plus more for garnish

instructions.text: Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 350°F. Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper liners. Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a medium bowl.

In another bowl, beat the eggs and both sugars with a mixer until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes. Gradually beat in the melted butter and vanilla. With the mixer on low speed, add half of the flour mixture, the milk and then the remaining flour. Fold in the peanuts but don't overmix.

Divide the batter evenly among the prepared cups, filling each about halfway. Bake until a toothpick inserted into a cupcake comes out clean, 20 to 22 minutes. Let cool in the pans 10 minutes, then transfer to racks to cool completely.

Make the nougat frosting: Beat the marshmallow crème, peanut butter and salt with a mixer until smooth; set aside. Make the chocolate frosting: Put both chocolates in a large microwave-safe bowl and microwave on 50 percent power until soft, about 1 minute. Stir, then continue to microwave until melted, 1 to 2 more minutes. Add the confectioners' sugar, milk, butter, vanilla and salt and beat with a mixer until smooth and creamy.
Spread nougat frosting over each cupcake, then top with chocolate frosting, leaving some of the nougat exposed. Garnish with peanuts.

recipes.title: Mint Patty Cakes

ingredients.item: vegetable shortening or cocoa butter, softened

instructions.text: Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 350°F. Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper liners. Put the butter, cocoa powder and 1/4 cup water in a medium microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave until the butter melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk to combine, then whisk in the brown sugar.

Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Whisk in the warm cocoa mixture. In another bowl, beat the buttermilk, eggs and vanilla; stir into the batter until just combined but don't overmix.

Divide the batter among the prepared cups, filling each about three-quarters of the way. Bake until the cupcakes spring back when touched, 30 to 35 minutes. Let cool in the pans 10 minutes, then transfer to racks to cool completely.

Make the topping: Beat the confectioners' sugar, corn syrup, shortening and peppermint extract with a mixer until a tight paste forms. Gather into a ball, place between two sheets of parchment paper and roll out to 1/4 inch thick (microwave 15 seconds to soften, if necessary). Use a 2 1/2-inch round cutter or juice glass to cut into disks; reroll the scraps. Place a peppermint disk on top of each cupcake.

Make the glaze: Put the chocolate, corn syrup, butter and 1/4 cup water in a microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave on 50 percent power until the chocolate melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk to combine, then cool slightly. Spread the glaze over the peppermint topping, leaving some peppermint exposed. Refrigerate until set, at least 20 minutes. Serve cold.

notes: Refrigerate until set, at least 20 minutes.
Serve cold.

instructions.text: Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 350°F using the convection setting, if available. Line a 24-cup mini muffin pan with paper liners. Combine the butter, cocoa powder and 1/4 cup water in a microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave until the butter melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk to combine, then whisk in the brown sugar.

Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Whisk in the warm cocoa mixture. In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg and vanilla; stir into the batter until just combined but don't overmix.

Divide the batter among the prepared cups, filling each three-quarters of the way. Bake until the cupcakes spring back when touched, about 20 minutes. Let cool in the pan 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

Make the topping: Bring the cream to a simmer in a small saucepan, then pour over the peanut butter chips in a bowl and let stand until the chips melt, about 5 minutes. Whisk until smooth. Refrigerate until the topping is set, about 10 minutes, then beat with a mixer until fluffy. Transfer to a pastry bag with a 1-inch round tip and pipe peaks onto each cupcake. Place in the freezer while you make the glaze.

Make the glaze: Put the butter, chocolate and 3 tablespoons hot water in a small, deep microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave on 50 percent power until the chocolate melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk until smooth. Dip the frozen peaks of each cupcake into the glaze, letting the excess drip off. Refrigerate until set, about 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Bob's Oatmeal-Crusted Trout

ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground pepper

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 300°F. Coarsely grind the oatmeal in a food processor. Transfer to a shallow dish and season with salt and pepper. Beat the egg and milk in another shallow dish.

Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp, about 8 minutes. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate. Remove and reserve all but about 2 tablespoons drippings from the skillet. Add the leeks and garlic to the skillet and cook until tender, about 5 minutes. Add the parsley, bacon, and salt and pepper to taste; keep warm.

Line a baking sheet with a double layer of paper towels. Dredge the trout in the oats, dip in the milk mixture and then in the oats again, turning to coat. Heat the reserved bacon drippings with the olive oil in another large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the trout in batches until golden on one side, about 3 minutes, then flip and fry until cooked through, about 2 more minutes. Transfer to the prepared baking sheet and keep warm in the oven. Add the vinegar to the skillet and bring to a boil. Serve the trout with the leeks and drizzle with the vinegar dressing.

notes: You can also try this recipe with salmon. - Bob Tuschman
I was inspired by Irish recipes, which often use oats for breading fish.

recipes.title: Claudia's Turkish Dumplings

ingredients.item: all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
small white onion, grated and squeezed dry

instructions.text: Make the dumplings: Cook the oatmeal as the label directs, then let cool. Combine the oatmeal, flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl and make a well in the center. Add the egg and olive oil to the well and mix with a fork. Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead into a smooth ball. Cover with a towel and let rest 30 minutes. Meanwhile, mix the beef, onion, 1 tablespoon salt, and pepper to taste in a bowl and set aside.

Prepare the toppings: Whisk the yogurt, garlic, 1/2 cup water, and salt to taste in a bowl. Heat the olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the pepper flakes and paprika and cook 1 minute. Set the yogurt sauce and spiced oil aside.

Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Divide the dough into 4 pieces. On a floured surface, roll each piece into a 20-by-4-inch rectangle, then cut into 2-inch squares. Place 1 teaspoon beef filling in the center of each square, fold over into a triangle and press the edges to seal.
Boil the dumplings in batches, stirring occasionally, until they float, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and transfer to bowls. Top with the yogurt sauce and spiced oil.

notes: I love manti, Turkish dumplings, with chili oil and yogurt. I thought it would be fun to try them with oatmeal! - Claudia Sidoti

instructions.text: Make the bark: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Combine the flour, oatmeal, walnuts, sugar and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and cook until light brown, 6 minutes. Stir into the dry ingredients. Press the dough into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan. Bake until golden brown, 30 minutes.
Remove the crust from the oven and sprinkle with the chocolate; let stand until soft, then spread with the back of a spoon. Refrigerate the bark until firm, 30 minutes. Break into pieces.

Make the oatmeal cream: Fill a large bowl with ice. Microwave 3/4 cup cream until simmering, 45 seconds. Puree with the oatmeal, sugar, a pinch of salt, vanilla and nutmeg in a blender. Transfer to a bowl and place over the ice; whisk until cool and thick. In another bowl, whisk the remaining 3/4 cup cream until soft peaks form; fold in the oatmeal puree.
Layer the oatmeal cream, bananas and crushed bark in 4 parfait glasses.

ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

instructions.text: Make the roasted garlic: Toss the 12 cloves garlic with the olive oil and 1 teaspoon water in a microwave-safe bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and microwave until soft, about 90 seconds. Let cool slightly, then peel.

Prepare the chili: Preheat the broiler. Cook the shallots in olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-low heat until caramelized, about 20 minutes. Meanwhile, place the chiles on a foil-lined broiler pan and broil until charred on all sides, turning about 8 minutes. Transfer to a bowl, cover with plastic wrap and let cool. Peel the peppers.

Add the minced garlic to the shallots and cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add the flour and cook, stirring, until lightly browned, about 3 minutes. Add the wine and stir with your fingers or a paring knife. Stir, then add the roasted garlic and chiles. Increase the heat to high and add the chicken broth; cook until slightly thickened.

Meanwhile, squeeze the soft pulp from the roasted garlic into a blender. Add the chile and the spinach and process until smooth. Add to the chili and stir. Add the beans, shredded chicken and chili powder. Simmer 30 minutes, adding cream at the end. Garnish with cheese.
